summary:
Project Overview:
COLLAPSE: IMMINENT is an interactive space survival strategy game based on a fictional human settlement on Mars. Players take on the responsibility of keeping the settlement alive when unexpected emergencies threaten its survival.
The settlement depends on limited resources such as oxygen, water, electricity and food. When emergencies like solar storms, power failures, oxygen system malfunctions and communication disruptions occur, players must make difficult decisions to protect the settlement.
Core Gameplay:
Resource Management: Players monitor and manage limited oxygen, water, electricity and food supplies.
Emergency Decisions: Unexpected situations force players to prioritise resources and choose between different solutions.
Chain Reaction: Every decision creates consequences. For example, diverting electricity from the greenhouse to repair the oxygen system may restore oxygen production but reduce future food supplies.
Mission Outcomes: Players can achieve survival, partial survival or mission failure depending on their decisions.
Mission Debrief: At the end, players receive an explanation of how their decisions affected the settlement.
Replay Option: Players can restart the mission and experiment with different strategies.

Scientific Foundation:

The game will incorporate real scientific concepts related to solar activity, space weather, radiation protection, life-support systems, energy management, water recycling and space agriculture. NASA resources such as DONKI, the Open Science Data Repository and Mars exploration research will help support scientific accuracy.

Visual and Technical Design:

The game features a cinematic space-themed introduction, an interactive mission dashboard, animated emergency alerts, resource indicators and decision-making screens. It is being developed as a browser-based interactive game using Google Antigravity, an AI-powered development platform. The platform supports the development process, helping us build and implement the game's interactive features and gameplay systems.

Team Responsibilities:

  • Game Development – Coding and implementing gameplay.
  • Scientific Research – NASA data and scientific accuracy.
  • Gameplay Design – Storyline, challenges and decision-making.
  • Visual Design – Interface, graphics and animations.
  • Testing and Presentation – Playtesting, improvements and final demonstration.
